# ClaudeCodeTemplate map

Version <code>v1.3.0</code>. The template turns Claude Code into a process: the rules live in <code>CLAUDE.md</code>, <b>skills</b> create the work (pitch, task, project), <b>agents</b> build it in the Execution Loop, and <b>hooks</b> stop whatever breaks the rules before it happens. This page is generated from <code>Template/</code> by <code>map/build.py</code>.

The full page, with dark mode and an index, is [index.html](index.html): open it in a browser. Legend: accent line: the main path; grey line: a call or trigger; red dashed line: a failure, block or rework; dotted line: optional or passive; box with dark border: template code (skills, agents, hooks); green-grey box: files and branches; light grey box: outside the project; dashed box: optional, or yours.

## The template in one picture

What it installs in a project: <code>CLAUDE.md</code> with the rules, 9 skills, 5 agents, hooks for 4 Claude Code events, a git hook, and 9 starter files in <code>docs/templates/</code>. At startup the session reads <code>CLAUDE.md</code>, <code>MEMORY.md</code>, <code>docs/SYSTEM.md</code> and the glossary, and confirms the template version. From then on it plans and orchestrates; the agents write the code.

![Overview: what the template installs in a project, and how the rules, the main session, the skills, the agents and the hooks connect.](svg/01-overview.svg)

*The frame is your repository. What comes in from the left is brought by template-sync; what sits on the right runs by itself (hooks) on every tool call, commit or push.*

## From idea to code

Work matures in three steps: a <b>Pitch</b> (a half-formed idea), a <b>Task</b> (one bounded change, one branch) and a <b>Project</b> (several scopes, with a spec package). All of that is planning: it is written and pushed on <code>dev</code>, in the primary checkout. Code is always written in a worktree per branch, inside <code>.claude/worktrees/</code>.

![Lifecycle of work: from an idea to a pitch, task or project, to the Execution Loop in a worktree, and from dev to tst and main.](svg/02-lifecycle.svg)

*A pitch ends as a task, a project, or archived. A task becomes a project when any of the 4 triggers fires: more than 3 scopes, more than one subsystem, a data model change, or a new external service. After the merge into dev, the item is marked [DONE] and its critical tests are promoted into TESTS.md.*

### Definition of Ready: what a task or scope needs before the implementer

Goal · Touches · Tasks · Acceptance Criteria · OUT of scope / No-gos · no Open Questions

## The Execution Loop

How every task or scope is built, from its worktree. The main session writes no code: it invokes the agents in order and commits once at the end, with the code, the cached tests and the docs together.

![Execution Loop: the steps of every task or scope, the agent that runs each one, the rework when review or test fails, and the BLOCKED path.](svg/03-execution-loop.svg)

*Boxes with a dark border are agents, with the model and effort from their frontmatter. The red line at the bottom is the rework, with one counter shared by review and test. At the top, the path when the implementer lacks information: it never guesses.*

<table><thead><tr><th>Agent</th><th>Model · effort</th><th>When</th><th>Tools</th><th>What it does</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>code-reviewer</code></td><td>opus · xhigh</td><td>3 · Review</td><td><code>Read, Glob, Grep, Bash</code></td><td>Reviews the diff: architecture, environments, simplicity, consistency, scope. <code>BLOCK</code> / <code>WARN</code> / <code>OK</code>.</td></tr><tr><td><code>doc-updater</code></td><td>sonnet · medium</td><td>6 · Document</td><td><code>Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash</code></td><td>Updates <code>docs/System/</code>, fixes what the change made false, regenerates the system map. Ends with <code>DOCS: …</code>.</td></tr><tr><td><code>docs-audit</code></td><td>opus · high</td><td>before dev → tst, or on demand</td><td><code>Read, Glob, Grep, Bash</code></td><td>Read-only: compares every checkable statement in the docs with the code.</td></tr><tr><td><code>implementer</code></td><td>sonnet · xhigh</td><td>2 · Implement, and every rework</td><td><code>Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Write, Edit</code></td><td>Writes the code for one task or scope. Returns <code>BLOCKED: &lt;question&gt;</code> when the Definition of Ready is not met. Never commits.</td></tr><tr><td><code>tester</code></td><td>opus · high</td><td>4 · Test, and regression before dev → tst</td><td><code>Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Write, Edit</code></td><td>Generates and caches scripts in <code>tests/cache/</code> from the declarative criteria, and <b>runs</b> them.</td></tr></tbody></table>

## Hooks: the hard gates

Hooks are scripts Claude Code runs by itself. <code>settings.json</code> points each event at a <code>dispatcher.sh</code> that is a fixed stub; all the logic lives in <code>lib/dispatch.sh</code>, so even an old template-sync can update it without breaking anything. Gates catch mechanical mistakes (wrong branch, secrets, missing docs); design judgment is left to the code-reviewer.

![Hooks: how a tool call goes through settings.json, the dispatcher and the runner, which runs every gate and combines their exit codes into allow, ask or deny.](svg/04-hooks.svg)

*The PreToolUse matcher is Bash|Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit: other tools never reach the gates. Your own hooks go in .claude/hooks/<type>/project/, and template-sync never touches them.*

<table><thead><tr><th>Hook</th><th>When</th><th>Effect</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>pre-tool/01-check-docs-before-push</code></td><td><code>git push</code></td><td>Deny when the unpushed commits change source but not the hand-written docs in <code>docs/System/</code> (the generated map does not count), unless they carry <code>Docs-Checked: no-changes — …</code>.</td></tr><tr><td><code>pre-tool/02-protected-branch</code></td><td>commit, merge, cherry-pick or revert on <code>main</code> / <code>master</code> / <code>tst</code>, or a push to one</td><td>Ask: your approval is the promotion or hotfix authorization.</td></tr><tr><td><code>pre-tool/03-no-secrets</code></td><td><code>git add</code>, <code>git commit</code></td><td>Deny when <code>.env</code>, <code>.deploy-secrets</code> or <code>docs/local/</code> are not ignored, are tracked or staged; also when <code>.claude/worktrees/</code> exists and is not ignored.</td></tr><tr><td><code>pre-tool/04-task-before-code</code></td><td>Edit / Write on code</td><td>Deny outside a <code>task-T-*</code> / <code>scope-P-*</code> branch whose task or project file exists. It does not see files written through Bash.</td></tr><tr><td><code>pre-tool/05-arch-check-before-push</code></td><td><code>git push</code></td><td>Deny when <code>.claude/arch-check.sh</code> exists and fails or is not executable.</td></tr><tr><td><code>session-start/01-template-update-check</code></td><td>a new session, or /clear</td><td>Tells Claude the version in use and, when a newer one is out, its CHANGELOG notes. Never changes anything.</td></tr><tr><td><code>.githooks/pre-commit</code></td><td>every commit, also outside Claude</td><td>Refuses commits that stage secrets. The backstop for 03.</td></tr></tbody></table>

### What gate 04 lets you edit without a task

docs/* · *.md · .claude/* · .gitignore · .githooks/* · tests/cache/*

## Branches and worktrees

- **<code>main</code>.** Production. Only receives merges from tst (with your approval) and hotfixes.
- **<code>tst</code>.** Staging. Receives dev when the project is complete, the regression tests pass and docs-audit reports no differences.
- **<code>dev</code>.** Integration and planning. The primary checkout lives here. Never code directly.
- **<code>task-T-xxxx-&lt;desc&gt;</code>.** One per task, from dev (from main/tst for a hotfix).
- **<code>scope-P-xxxx-N-&lt;desc&gt;</code>.** One per project scope, from dev.
- **<code>.claude/worktrees/&lt;branch&gt;</code>.** One worktree per code branch, gitignored. Removed after the merge.

<table><thead><tr><th>What changes</th><th>Committed on</th><th>By</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Pitches, tasks, projects, glossary and their INDEX</td><td><code>dev</code>, as written</td><td>planning skills</td></tr><tr><td>Spec/task fixes after a BLOCKED</td><td><code>dev</code>, then <code>git merge dev</code> into the branch</td><td>main session</td></tr><tr><td>Code + docs/System + map</td><td>the task/scope branch</td><td>main session (Execution Loop)</td></tr><tr><td>Docs fixes with no code change (from docs-audit)</td><td><code>dev</code></td><td>main session</td></tr><tr><td>Status [IN PROGRESS] / [DONE], INDEX, TESTS.md</td><td><code>dev</code>, right after the merge</td><td>main session</td></tr></tbody></table>

## Template updates

Each project keeps its template version on line 1 of <code>CLAUDE.md</code>. When a session starts, the hook compares it with the CHANGELOG on <code>main</code> and, if the project is behind, shows you the release notes. Only when you say yes does <code>template-sync</code> run; it also repairs projects half-upgraded by older versions.

![Updates: the session-start hook announces a newer version; template-sync, only after your yes, replaces the template&#x27;s files and never yours.](svg/05-updates.svg)

*The manifest (.claude/.template-manifest) defines what the template owns. seed entries (.claude/skills/deployment-process/SKILL.md) are copied only when missing: the project adapts them. To turn the notice off: CLAUDE_TEMPLATE_UPDATE_CHECK=0.*

## How this map stays current

Generated by <code>map/build.py</code>, with the engine of the <code>system-map</code> skill: never edit <code>map/README.md</code>, <code>map/index.html</code> or <code>map/svg/</code> by hand. <code>facts.py</code> reads the version, skills, agents (model, effort and tools from their frontmatter), hooks and Execution Loop steps from <code>Template/</code>. <code>python3 map/build.py --check</code> fails when the committed map is stale, when the template has something the figures do not draw, or when a hook stops doing what the map says; the message names the file to edit.
